newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda's T-bill discount rate up on easing demand.
newsitem.headline: Uganda's T-bill discount rate up on easing demand.

text.p: The discount rate on Uganda's main group of treasury bills rose last week after demand fell, the central Bank of Uganda said on Monday.
The bank said the discount rate on 91-day bills rose to 11.5 percent from 11.32 percent.
"After remaining stable for three weeks running, demand eased a bit, hence the slight fall," a bank official said.

Constant demand kept the discount rate and average weighted price for the 91-day bills constant for three weeks, for the first time since the bill sales were introduced by the reformist government of President Yoweri Museveni in 1993.
The bank said average weighted price for the bills fell slightly to 97.13 at the auction, from 97.18 previously.
BOU auctions the 91-day bills daily to mostly commercial banks, insurance firms and the national social security fund.
It said in a statement some three billion shillings ($2.84 million) had been put up for sale at the auction. All the bills were bought. The same amount would be auctioned this week.
The bank auctions 182, 273 and 364-day bills monthly.
